method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: the compilation published on legislation.wa.gov.au (mrdoc 45283; no compilation number given; compilation table ends with the Legal Profession Uniform Law Application Act 2022 Pt 17 Div 5, in force 1 July 2022), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/mrdoc_45283.txt (retrieved 2026-09-07); no regulations set its numbers

scope: From the seat of a party to a domestic commercial arbitration or to a dispute mediated by an arbitrator. Domestic commercial arbitration and where the Act applies (s 1(1)-(3)); definition and form of arbitration agreement (s 7); referral by a court (s 8(1)); number and appointment of arbitrators (ss 10, 11(2)-(4)); challenge (s 12(3), (4), (6)); equal treatment and the right to be heard (ss 18, 24(2)-(5)); arbitrator as mediator (s 27D(1), (4)-(6)); settlement and award on agreed terms (s 30); reasons (s 31(3)); correction within 30 days (s 33(1)(a)); setting aside and the 3-month limit (s 34(1)-(3)); appeal on a question of law by agreement and leave (s 34A(1), (3), (6)); recognition and enforcement (ss 35, 36(1)). Not encoded: Part 1A, ss 2A-6, 9, Part 4A, ss 12(1)-(2), 13-16, 19-23, 24A-27C, 27E-29, 32, 33(2)-(8), 33A-33F, 34(4), 34A(4)-(11), 36(2), Parts 9-11; costs agreements (Legal Profession Uniform Law); enforcement of settlements outside arbitration (general law of contract and deeds).
seat: a party to a domestic commercial arbitration, or to a dispute mediated by an arbitrator under s 27D
